recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-7518 unless the Public Health work group reopens the later protocolApplied or targetDisease cardinality decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-7518 was a Published FHIR-core Immunization change request with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution. The ballot comment questioned why Immunization.vaccinationProtocol was 0..*; the recorded multivalent-vaccine examples supported repeatable protocol entries and the applied modification changed doseTarget/targetDisease handling and SNOMED target-disease terminology.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by 2015 commits 4e6d62c693, e43671d5b7, and bde793d48a, which kept vaccinationProtocol repeatable, changed doseTarget/targetDisease from 1..1 to 1..*, renamed doseTarget to targetDisease with FHIR-7519, and updated the target disease value set toward SNOMED CT disease concepts.
additional_context: Immunization is active in source/fhir.ini. Later published decisions changed the same model: FHIR-8406 removed the old vaccinationProtocol backbone for R4, FHIR-16520 reintroduced protocolApplied as 0..*, FHIR-19487 changed protocolApplied.targetDisease to no minimum cardinality, and FHIR-15972 refined the target disease example value set.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source has Immunization.protocolApplied 0..* and a SNOMED CT-based Immunization Target Disease value set, preserving the applicable parts of FHIR-7518. Current targetDisease 0..* is intentional under later FHIR-19487 and should not be reverted to FHIR-7518's earlier 1..* application.

related_jiras.note: Removed the old vaccinationProtocol backbone and reframed protocol modeling before R4.
Reintroduced Immunization.protocolApplied as 0..* after FHIR-8406 removed vaccinationProtocol.
Superseded FHIR-7518's targetDisease minimum by making protocolApplied.targetDisease optional.
Refined the target disease example value set that descended from FHIR-7518's SNOMED target-disease work.
